options.metric: Annual count of reported motorist deaths
options.reason: A direct count shows whether the annual number of motorists killed in reported NYC crashes changed over time.
options.answer: Reported motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (26.4%), but this crash data cannot establish whether per-mile risk declined.
options.interpretation: This answers whether the annual burden of reported motorist deaths was lower at the endpoints: it fell 26.4%, despite intervening fluctuations. Annual counts are directly measured and easy to interpret, but without annual miles driven they leave the requested per-mile risk unanswered.

options.metric: Crashes with at least one motorist death per 100,000 reported crashes
options.denominator: All reported crash records in the same year
options.reason: A crash-level rate adjusts for changes in the annual volume of crash records and compares the frequency of fatal crashes over time.
options.answer: Crashes with a motorist death increased from 50.1 to 87.7 per 100,000 reported crashes between 2013 and 2025 (75.1%), but this does not determine per-mile risk.
options.interpretation: This answers how often a reported crash involved at least one motorist death: the frequency increased from 50.1 to 87.7 per 100,000 crashes between 2013 and 2025. It adjusts for annual crash-report volume, a defensible crash-level comparison, but leaves per-mile risk unanswered because the data do not include vehicle-miles traveled.
